question.worked_solution:
Let $u=2x-1.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that $x=\frac{u+1}{2}.$

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\sqrt{2x-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{u+1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{u}\cdot (\frac{1}{2})\text{d}u \\  & =\int \frac{u\sqrt{u}+\sqrt{u}}{4}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int ({u}^{3/2}+{u}^{1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (\frac{2}{5}{u}^{5/2}+\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{10}(2x-1)^{5/2}+\frac{1}{6}(2x-1)^{3/2}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\sqrt{(2x-1)^{5}}+\frac{1}{6}\sqrt{(2x-1)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$
